detail: ticket 2: first merge passed, 0 merge failure(s), 9 steps; recall showed 4 fact(s)

memories_after: [Fact] In the docs project worktree, document file contents are verified by reading them back with PowerShell's 'Get-Content -Raw'.
[Fact] In the docs project, new files are confirmed as untracked-but-present via 'git status --short' (showing a '??' entry for the new directory).
[Fact] In the docs project, the reports/ directory may not exist in the worktree initially and is created implicitly by writing a file such as reports/weekly.txt into it.

[Lesson] In the docs project, a worktree may not contain agenium.toml, and agenium.toml has [checks] pre_merge empty when present; pre-merge checks still run, so never assume absence of visible check config means no checks exist.
[Fact] On Windows worktrees in this environment, verifying files with PowerShell (Test-Path, Get-Content, -ceq, -match) and git status/git diff works well.
[Fact] In the docs project, deliverables/ and reports/ are the directories where team documents live, as stated in README.md.
[Fact] In the docs project, the first line of every team document in deliverables/ or reports/ must be exactly 'Owner: docs-team'; a pre-merge check enforces this.

[Lesson] Meeting a ticket's literal acceptance criteria (file exists, contains the word) is not enough in the docs project; project-wide document conventions such as the owner first line are also enforced before merge.
